issues.summary: The household's records live in one dynamic structure: kinds as data, records as documents, history as events, figures as views
issues.description:
As the developer I want the household's records kept in one dynamic structure so that a new kind of asset, debt or account needs no new table and no migration.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/registry/`; ARCHITECTURE.md 4.

**Keys built for the questions the household will ask** (Arun, 24 Oct 2026: "I will be making such queries in future about my transactions and investments"). One table, every item under the household; records, events and views are each keyed so that every question below is a single Query, never a Scan. The questions are:

* last month's transactions for the household;
* my transactions this year;
* every transaction on one holding or loan;
* dividends or fees in a date range;
* a holding's valuation history;
* the changes one member made.

Dates are ISO, so key order is date order.

**Acceptance.**

* Kinds are data: each kind is a versioned spec, and a record names its kind and version.
* Records are documents: each record carries its kind, version, owners with their shares, country, currency, liquidity, status, parent, instrument and attributes, keyed by the household (ARCHITECTURE.md 4).
* History is events: every change, a correction made in place included, is appended as an event with who and when; nothing is overwritten.
* Figures are views: every figure is a view rebuilt from the events, and a test rebuilds each view from scratch and gets the same figures.
* No migration for a new kind: adding a kind's spec is enough, with no new table and no code change to the store (test).
* A repository function serves each question above, and a test proves each one is a single Query with the right key condition. A test fails if the registry layer ever calls Scan.
* ARCHITECTURE.md §4 records the structure. A seed command loads the first record.
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest.

**Depends on.**

* MA-24
* MA-26

Updated 26 Oct 2026 (MA-186): the fixed entities and their key table give way to one dynamic structure: kinds as data, records as documents, history as events, figures as views.

**Stack (MA-265).** The registry is a thin typed single-table repository in `src/mypaisa_agent/registry/` built directly on Pydantic v2 models (`Kind`, `Record`, `Event`, `Commitment`, `PlanItem`, `View`), `boto3`'s `dynamodb` client and resource (`TypeSerializer` and `TypeDeserializer` with `Decimal` conversion at the wire boundary), and `mypy-boto3-dynamodb` (`boto3-stubs[dynamodb]`) under strict `pyright`. No ORM (PynamoDB) and no Amazon DocumentDB (`docs/RESEARCH.md` §6.2).

issues.summary: The second check: a fresh Sign in with Apple or passkey under Face ID, or Google again for a Google-only member, bound to the action and verified by the server
issues.description:
As a member I want an action that matters to need more than an unlocked phone or an open browser, so that a stolen or borrowed device cannot change the household's members, its kinds or its settings.

**Where.** `handlers/api` (the challenge and the check), `src/mypaisa_agent/auth/`, the iOS app's second check sheet (a SwiftUI piece in the React Native shell, MA-165), the board `Second check` in `iPhone admin.dc.html` (MyPaisa iOS v1); `web/` (the web app's second check). ARCHITECTURE.md §4.5.

**Acceptance.**

* **Phase 1, with sign-in.** The challenge and the check ship with sign-in at both doors (Arun, 26 Oct 2026), so approving a new kind can sit behind it from phase 2 (MA-197); the Admin center (phase 8, MA-184) and the imports (phase 9, MA-111) reuse the same api routes, challenge and check.
* **What it covers, exactly** (ARCHITECTURE.md §4.5, "The second check"): the owner's admin actions, from the Admin center or the admin's chat (ARCHITECTURE.md §20.3); an import's Confirm and rolling an import back; leaving the household (MA-172); approving a new kind (MA-197); and nothing else.
* **The challenge.** A Confirm on one of those actions asks the server for a challenge bound to that action.
* **The assertion, in the iOS app.** A fresh one: Sign in with Apple again (iOS shows a Face ID sheet) or, where the member added one, a passkey (Face ID); a member who signs in only with Google proves it with Google again.
* **The assertion, in the web app.** A passkey or a fresh Apple or Google sign-in in the browser.
* **The check.** The server accepts the action only with an assertion under five minutes old, from that member, whose nonce is that challenge; anything else is refused and nothing changes. Cancelling cancels the action.
* **Never local only.** A local Face ID check (the app lock, MA-171) never authorises anything on the server.
* **Audit.** Every sign-in and every second check, passed or failed, is an audit row; signing in on a device or a browser the member has not used before sends a push to their other devices and a card in their chat ("New sign-in to MyPaisa: an iPad, with Google, today at 19:41. Was this you?", with Yes, it was me and No, sign it out, which signs that device out); until the member answers, Members and devices shows it as not confirmed, and the owner's chat gets one line with Open Admin center (ARCHITECTURE.md §4.5, "A new device", MA-102); a failed check tells the owner.
* **Tests:**

    * a valid assertion, one older than five minutes, a nonce from another challenge, a replay, cancel;
    * another member's assertion, a member of another household, and a removed or paused member;
    * a Google-only member;
    * a passkey registered in one environment and tried in the other;
    * each action in the set asks for the check (an admin action from the admin's chat as well as from the Admin center, and approving a new kind), and no other action does;
    * each case from the browser as well as the app.
    
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest; the iOS gates (MA-166); Playwright for the web app's check.

**Depends on.**

* MA-75
* MA-109
* MA-168

**How.**

1. **The template.** A versioned workbook with one sheet each for Accounts, Holdings, Transactions and Valuations. It has dropdown lists and built-in checks. It carries the years of investment history; the budget and the plans are set up through the chat, not imported.
2. **Sending it.** Either the owner sends the .xlsx in the chat, from Files or the share sheet, or Claude Code on the owner's laptop uploads it through a one-time link: the owner taps **Upload from my laptop** in the chat, and the app shows a link that accepts one .xlsx of at most 20 MB within 15 minutes, then expires.     * A whole import can be rolled back by its id, which is itself confirmed with the second check and audited.

* A test workbook of 10,000 transactions passes the dry run in under a minute, and its writes stay inside DynamoDB's limits, with batching and backoff.

issues.summary: The chat sends Claude only the current conversation, kept short, with notes on recent ones
issues.description:
As a member I want MyPaisa to remember what we were just talking about without re-reading months of chat, so that each message costs pennies and the context never runs out.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/agent.py`, the `ChatTurn` item, `ARCHITECTURE.md` §8.

**Acceptance.**

* Every message is stored as one `ChatTurn` row, with the response's content blocks exactly as returned. Rows are kept 90 days, and earlier turns are never edited or trimmed.
* When conversations end:

    * a conversation ends after 30 minutes of silence, or when a guided flow finishes;
    * it stays open while an `ask_user` question waits, for up to the `PendingAction`'s day.
    
* A new conversation starts from the cached fixed part (system prompt, tools, rubrics) plus a few one-line notes on the member's recent conversations. Haiku writes those notes when each conversation closes.
* The notes sit after the cached part, so members share the cache.
* A conversation past about 50,000 tokens starts afresh from a summary.
* The fixed part is cached with the one-hour TTL.
* `tool_choice` is always `auto`, and tools are `strict: true`.
* Tests:

    * the stored history replays byte for byte;
    * a conversation closes at 30 minutes, but not while a question waits;
    * the notes are built and sent;
    * `cache_read_input_tokens` is above zero on the second message.
    
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest.

issues.summary: F1: ten years of point-in-time market, economy and world-event data sit in one queryable store
issues.description:
As the developer I want ten years of history stored as it was known on each day, so that every model and backtest sees only what was knowable then.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/forecaster/data/`, the `mypaisa-<env>-lake` S3 bucket (Parquet), DuckDB, `infra/modules/mypaisa`. Sources and prices: `ARCHITECTURE.md` §19.2.

**Acceptance.**

* **Sources are free first** (Arun, 24 Oct 2026): yfinance, Twelve Data's free tier, and free websites where their terms allow. EODHD is used only when the data steward (MA-131) shows that no free source can serve a holding, and the admin approves.
* Stored from 2015, or from inception if later, from those sources:

    * **Shares, ETFs and commodity ETCs:** daily open, high, low, close and volume.
    * **UK funds (OEICs):** the daily price only. Yahoo's `0P...` id first, then the fund manager's page; EODHD `.EUFUND` by ISIN only if approved.
    * **Constituents and indexes:** each fund's top holdings and the index it tracks.
    * **Commodity drivers:** gold, silver, Brent and WTI futures (yfinance), and daily Brent and WTI from the EIA.
    * **Economy:** from FRED with its ALFRED archive, so each figure is stored as first published, plus the Bank of England, the ECB and the ONS.
    * **Market stress:** VIX, credit spreads, the dollar index.
    * **World events:** GDELT daily event counts and tone by country and theme, and the geopolitical risk index.
    * **Calendars:** central bank decisions, inflation releases and earnings.
    
* Each source is a setting (MA-129), so its order and use can be changed from the admin desk.
* Each holding gets an **exposure map**, stored on the instrument's `exposure` and refreshed on its own schedule:

    * funds and ETFs: top holdings, countries, sectors and currencies, from factsheets and holdings files (monthly; iShares daily);
    * shares: the company, its sector, main markets, suppliers and rivals (quarterly);
    * commodities: their fixed list of drivers (reviewed yearly);
    * cash: its rate and currency.
    
* Every row carries the date it became known. Revisions are added, never overwritten.
* A daily refresh runs after the close. A gap or a stale feed raises an alarm in the chat.
* Each source's licence is recorded; personal use only.
* Tests:

    * no feature is ever used before its known date;
    * the refresh is idempotent;
    * backfill totals reconcile with the sources;
    * each kind's exposure map is built from fixtures.
    
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest, terraform validate.

**Depends on.** MA-11 (phase 10 prices), MA-104 (the Parquet and DuckDB copy).

issues.summary: F3: the Forecaster names the market's mood and forecasts the next four weeks' risk
issues.description:
As the owner I want to know whether the market is calm, choppy, stressed or falling, and how rough the next four weeks could be for each holding, so that I can avoid the deep falls.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/forecaster/models/regime.py`, `risk.py`; the `Forecast` and `ModelVersion` items.

**Acceptance.**

* **Market mood:** each day gets a mood (calm and rising, choppy, stressed, falling) with its probability, from a regime model over the cross-asset features. The mood must not flip back and forth day to day.
* **Risk:** each holding gets a four-week volatility forecast and the chance of a fall over 5%. It comes from a volatility model and gradient-boosted trees, combined and calibrated.
* In walk-forward tests over the ten years, the chance of a fall over 5% beats the historical base rate on Brier score.
* Every forecast is stored and graded when its four weeks are up. It runs in shadow until F6's gate.
* Tests:

    * walk-forward folds leave a gap so no training window overlaps a test window;
    * the calibration curve is checked;
    * the mood stays stable.
    
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest.

**Depends on.** F1, F2.

issues.summary: F4: similar past days and a library of event impacts explain what usually happened next
issues.description:
As the owner I want each day's news, events and world politics checked against what I actually hold, and to see how my holdings moved after past events like them, so that a forecast comes with evidence I can read.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/forecaster/models/analogs.py`, `events.py`, `news_match.py`; the `ArticleScore` item; `ARCHITECTURE.md` §19.3 and §19.4.

**Acceptance.**

* **Similar days:** each day is described by a set of features (trend, momentum, volatility, drawdown, cross-asset mood, macro surprises, news tone).

    * The 30 nearest days since 2015 are found, leaving out the last 20 days.
    * The engine reports how those days played out after 5, 20 and 60 days.
    
* **Matching news to holdings:**

    * Each day's stories come from GDELT, the RSS feeds and EODHD's news feed.
    * Claude Haiku tags each story through Batches with:
    
        * the companies, countries, sectors, commodities and central banks it names;
        * its event type;
        * the direction it points.
        
    * Each story's relevance to each holding is worked out in code: the holding's exposure weights (from its F1 exposure map) on the entities the story names. Some examples:
    
        * a chip-export story reaches a NASDAQ fund through its chipmaker weight;
        * an OPEC+ cut reaches an oil holding through its first driver;
        * a Fed surprise reaches gold through real yields and the dollar.
        
    * Stories below a relevance floor are dropped.
    * Matches are stored on `ArticleScore` as `entities[]`, `event_type` and `matches[]`.
    * The matches feed the event-impact lookup, the F5 forecast and the morning brief ("3 stories touch your holdings today"). News alone never raises a red alert.
    
* **Event impacts:**

    * Event types: rate decision surprise, inflation surprise, election, armed conflict escalation, tariffs or sanctions, pandemic shock, earnings miss of a top holding, OPEC+ decision.
    * For each holding and type: the measured average move and spread after 1, 5 and 20 days, the number of cases, and a confidence interval.
    * Fewer than 8 cases are marked low confidence.
    * The impact numbers always come from code.
    
* **Checking the tags:** they are checked weekly on a labelled sample. If tagging falls short, Marketaux's per-company sentiment (about $29 a month) is the fallback, decided then.
* Tests:

    * the similar-days search never uses the future;
    * the event study matches a hand-worked example;
    * the relevance score on fixtures for a fund, a share and a commodity;
    * the classifier on a labelled set.
    
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest.

**Depends on.** F1 (MA-119), MA-16 (phase 14 news).

issues.summary: E5: confidence is recalibrated every day within safe bounds, and rolled back on its own if it gets worse
issues.description:
As the owner I want the confidence numbers retuned every day from the latest graded results, without lurching on one noisy day, so that "70%" keeps meaning 70%.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/learning/calibrate.py`, the `CalibrationMap` item and `calibration/` in S3; `ARCHITECTURE.md` §20.4.

**Acceptance.**

* **Daily refit:** each day, a calibration map for the rules engine and for each Forecaster model is refitted on a rolling window. Its settings:

    * window length;
    * the minimum number of graded predictions per bucket;
    * the most any bucket may move in one day (2 points by default).
    
* **When a new map is used:** only if it scores better than the current map on the held-back part of the window, within the automatic band of E1. It is a new version, and the admin sees it in the daily digest.
* **Probation:** a new map is watched for 10 trading days. If its live Brier score is worse than the previous map's by more than the tolerance, it is rolled back on its own and the admin is told.
* **What it does not touch:** rule thresholds or model structure.
* **Tests:**

    * the daily step limit;
    * too few cases leaves the map unchanged;
    * the rollback;
    * a replay over ten years shows calibration stays within tolerance.
    
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest.

**Depends on.** E4.

issues.summary: Each member's messages travel through ordered queues, in and out, are retried with backoff and are never lost
issues.description:
As a member I want every message I send and every message MyPaisa sends me handled in order and retried if something fails, so that nothing I say is dropped and nothing is answered out of turn.

**Where.**

* the chat API (`handlers/api`, MA-31), the `agent` and `sender` handlers;
* `mypaisa-<env>-updates.fifo` and `mypaisa-<env>-outbox.fifo` with their dead-letter queues;
* `infra/modules/mypaisa`;
* `ARCHITECTURE.md` §21.

**Acceptance.**

* **Inbound:**

    * The chat API checks the member's token (MA-75), then puts the message or tap on `updates.fifo`. The message group is the member; the deduplication id is the app's client id.
    * It answers the app with `202` at once.
    * The agent takes each member's messages one at a time, in order. Different members run in parallel.
    
* **Outbound:**

    * Every message, card and edit MyPaisa sends goes on `outbox.fifo`, with the member as the message group.
    * A `sender` handler delivers them in order over the member's stream on the api host (MA-30), and by push when the member has no presence (MA-170). It honours API Gateway's and APNs' throttling (`retry_after`) and stays under their limits.
    * Taps on a card's buttons are still acknowledged at once.
    
* **Retries:**

    * Inbound: 3 tries within about a minute, so a member's lane is never stuck for long.
    * Outbound: 5 tries.
    * The backoff comes from settings.
    * An error that cannot succeed goes straight to the dead-letter queue with its reason. A wrong format or an unknown member are examples.
    
* **Idempotency:** every handler is idempotent by client id or message id (Powertools idempotency), so a retry never does anything twice.
* **Dead-letter queues:** after the last try, a message moves to its dead-letter queue, and the member is told: "That did not go through; I have kept it and will try again."

    * Messages are kept 14 days, with a copy in S3 for good.
    * Each dead-letter queue has an alarm when it holds anything, which alerts the admin through the router (MA-137).
    
* **Replaying:** `scripts/redrive.sh <queue>` moves dead-lettered messages back.

    * A message older than an hour is answered with "still want this?" instead of being acted on.
    * A Confirm tap whose `PendingAction` has expired is refused.
    
* **Concurrency:** reserved concurrency on the agent keeps Anthropic calls and spend in bounds.
* **Tests:**

    * order within a lane while lanes run in parallel;
    * a duplicate client id ignored;
    * backoff and the move to the dead-letter queue;
    * the alarm;
    * a replayed old message asking first;
    * an expired Confirm refused;
    * 429 handling in the sender.
    
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest, terraform validate.

**Depends on.** MA-31, MA-30, MA-138.

Updated 25 Oct 2026 (MA-161): Telegram's webhook, `update_id` and rate limits give way to the app's chat API with its client id, and the sender delivers to the stream on the api host and by push.

issues.summary: The ops warden replays dead-lettered work on its own once the cause is healthy, and opens an incident if it fails again
issues.description:
As the admin I want failed work replayed without me once whatever broke it is healthy again, so that an APNs, Anthropic or data-source outage heals on its own and only a repeat failure reaches me.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/agents/ops_warden.py`; the dead-letter queues of MA-139 and MA-140; the `Incident` item; the replay limits as settings (MA-129). PLAN.md phase 18 (E7: dead-lettered work replayed on its own once its cause is healthy, at most three times, then an incident); ARCHITECTURE.md §20.5 and §21.3. MA-135 builds the warden and the daily state machine; this story adds the automatic replay its description does not yet hold.

**Acceptance.**

* When a dead-letter queue holds anything, the warden reads the reasons and names the cause: APNs or the stream on the api host, the Anthropic API, a data source or a deploy.
* It checks that cause's health with a cheap probe and replays only once it is healthy again.
* At most three replays per message, with growing gaps. The limits are settings inside their band (E1).
* A message that fails the same way again becomes an `Incident` on the admin desk with its errors attached, and is not replayed again without the admin.
* Every automatic replay goes in the daily digest and writes an audit row. The \[Replay\] button (phase 8) and `scripts/redrive.sh` keep working beside it.
* Replays stay safe: idempotent handlers, "still want this?" for messages more than an hour old, expired Confirms refused.
* Tests: an injected outage that recovers is replayed once; a cause still down is not replayed; the third failure opens an incident; replay is idempotent; the limits are read from settings.
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest.

**Depends on.** MA-135, MA-139, MA-140, MA-129, MA-130.

issues.summary: Every file and image a member sends is kept in S3 for good, with a Document row and an audit entry that point to it
issues.description:
As the owner I want every file and image anyone in the household sends in the app kept in S3 and linked from the audit log, so that the original behind any change can always be looked at again.

Arun, 24 Oct 2026: "Remember all the files and images I send should be stored on S3 and I should be able to view that in audit logs." This replaces the earlier rule that screenshots were deleted after extraction unless the member said keep.

**Where.** The chat API's presigned upload (`handlers/api`, MA-31), `handlers/agent` and the docs job of `handlers/worker`; the `mypaisa-<env>-documents` bucket in `infra/modules/mypaisa`; the `Document` and `AuditEvent` items. ARCHITECTURE.md §4.1, §4.6 and §14; PLAN.md phase 1.

**Acceptance.**

* Every file a member sends (PDF, image, CSV, spreadsheet, CAS statement) goes from the app straight to `s3://mypaisa-<env>-documents/<household>/<member>/<yyyy>/<mm>/<document_id>.<ext>` through a short-lived presigned upload, before anything reads it, whatever happens next: read, rejected, cancelled or failed.
* Each file gets a `Document` row: `document_id`, `s3_key`, `sha256`, `mime`, `bytes`, `original_name`, `sent_by`, `sent_at`, the message's client id, `kind` (`factsheet`, `screenshot`, `cas`, `broker_export`, `spreadsheet`, `other`), and the instrument or import it ended up feeding, if any. A file sent twice is recognised by its `sha256` and linked, not stored twice.
* An `AuditEvent` for the upload itself (`entity` Document, `action` create, `via` the file's kind), and every change made from a file carries its `document_id`, so the audit log can show the source file of each change.
* Never deleted: no expiry rule on the bucket; versioning and `prevent_destroy` in prod; public access blocked; encrypted at rest; only the docs job and the api Lambda may read it, each in its own environment; the app may only write a new object through its presigned link.
* Passwords for protected PDFs are never stored, logged or sent to Claude; extracted records never keep a PAN, an address or account numbers, even though the file itself is kept as sent.
* Dev holds synthetic files only.
* Tests: a file stored before extraction; a failed extraction still stored; a duplicate linked by hash; the audit rows; no PAN in any extracted record; a presigned link that cannot overwrite or read.
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest with moto, terraform fmt and validate, tflint.

**Depends on.** MA-26, MA-27, MA-28, MA-37

## What and why

`MA-265` evaluated six agent frameworks and selected a thin, custom-typed `AnthropicAgentRunner` (\~250 lines of Python over `anthropic.AsyncAnthropic` + Pydantic v2) for the interactive `agent` Lambda. That keeps first-class control over:

* prompt caching for every agent (`cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"}`, ARCHITECTURE 24.1);
* PDF document blocks and citations;
* the in-loop policy gate (`MA-247`) and the post-loop figure validator (`MA-248`);
* `gen_ai.*` OpenTelemetry spans (`MA-233`).

This story builds that core runner and `@tool` schema registry. Every later agent is built on it, so caching and memory come from here (ARCHITECTURE 24, MA-285).

## Where in the repo

* `src/mypaisa/agent/runner.py`
* `src/mypaisa/agent/tools.py`
* `src/mypaisa/agent/cache.py`
* `tests/test_agent_runner.py`

## Acceptance criteria

* \[ \] **Typed** `@tool` **Registry & Pydantic v2 Schema Export.** Declares every tool with `@tool(agents=[...], scope="read"|"propose"|"write", allowed_when_tainted=bool)` and generates strict JSON Schemas matching the manifest checked by `MA-246`.
* \[ \] **Prompt Cache Assembler, for every agent** (ARCHITECTURE 24.1, updated 29 Oct 2026 by MA-285).

    * Builds every request in one frozen order: tools sorted by name and serialised deterministically, then the system prompt with the kind templates, then the messages.
    * Places at most three explicit `cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"}` breakpoints: (1) the tools and system prompt together, (2) the household structure snapshot, (3) the conversation notes.
    * Leaves the fourth slot to the request's top-level automatic caching for the conversation's tail; four explicit breakpoints plus automatic caching would be a 400.
    * Takes each agent's cache lifetime from its manifest (the chat's fixed part 1h, its tail 5m).
    * Keeps the warm-turn cache hit ratio above 75%. MA-286 adds the byte test, T1's read check and the panel's alarm.
    
* \[ \] **Async Tool-Use Loop with Policy & Figure Hooks.** Runs the `messages.stream` / `messages.create` loop up to the per-run step cap. Passes every `tool_use` block through the policy gate (`MA-247`) before execution, runs the figure validator (`MA-248`) on the final reply before emitting to `mypaisa-<env>-out.fifo`, and enforces the monthly budget ceiling (`MA-113`).
* \[ \] **Automatic** `gen_ai.*` **&** `mypaisa.*` **Span Emission.** Wraps every model turn and tool call in OpenTelemetry spans. Each records the model ID, input and output tokens, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `ttft_ms`, `cost_usd` and `stop_reason`, with zero message content (`MA-233`).

## Gates

* `python3 scripts/plan_sync.py selftest && python3 scripts/plan_sync.py check`
* `pytest tests/test_agent_runner.py`

issues.summary: Every agent's model calls are cached automatically: a frozen prefix, a lifetime per route, automatic caching for the tail, and an alarm when reads fall
issues.description:
As the admin I want every agent MyPaisa builds to cache its prompt without anyone remembering to, so that each call pays for its fixed part once and the Claude budget lasts.

**What.** The runner (`AnthropicAgentRunner`, MA-271) makes the request for every agent, so caching lives there once (ARCHITECTURE 24.1):

* **One order, frozen.** Tools sorted by name and serialised deterministically, then the system prompt, then the messages. Nothing that changes per member, per day or per request sits before the first breakpoint: no date, no member name, no id, no figure, no unsorted JSON.
* **Dynamic context goes after the cache.** Today's date, the member's name and mode, privacy mode and the ladder's step arrive as a mid-conversation system message, after the cached prefix. Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 support this with no beta.
* **Breakpoints.** At most three explicit breakpoints at the stable layers: tools and system together, then the household's layer, then the notes. Top-level automatic caching (`cache_control` on the request) takes the conversation's tail, the fourth slot.
* **A lifetime per route.** Each agent's manifest (MA-246) names its time to live from how far apart its calls start. Under 5 minutes takes 5m; 5 to 60 minutes takes 1h, longer first. The chat's fixed part is 1h, as ARCHITECTURE 8 says, and its tail 5m. A daily or weekly run takes 5m within the run. Batches mark their shared prefix too.
* **One model per loop.** Caches belong to a model, so a loop never switches models mid-run. A cheaper sub-task is its own call.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/agent/cache.py` and `runner.py`, each agent's manifest, the model panel and its alarms (MA-233), the T1 golden set (MA-250).

**Acceptance.**

* A unit test builds every agent's request twice (two members, two days, two runs) and asserts the bytes before the first breakpoint are identical. No date, id, name, figure or unsorted key leaks in.
* A manifest with no time to live, or more than three explicit breakpoints, fails the build.
* In T1 (evals workspace), the second identical request of each agent shows `cache_read_input_tokens` above zero.
* Every `RunRecord` holds the cache read and write tokens per call. The model panel shows the cache-read share per agent. An alarm fires once when an agent's share falls out of its band for a day.
* In dev, cache diagnostics (beta `cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07`, Claude API only) names where a broken prefix first differs.
* The Console's caching analytics for the dev and prod workspaces show reads once traffic runs. That is the second place to look, beside the panel.

**Depends on.** MA-271, MA-233, MA-246, MA-250.

**Gates.** `uv run ruff check . && uv run pyright && uv run pytest`; T1 on the change.

issues.summary: Every agent keeps memory across runs through Claude's memory tool on MyPaisa's own store, scoped, guarded and audited, and long runs stay lean
issues.description:
As a member I want MyPaisa to remember what I told it last week, such as how I like answers and what I am planning, without my repeating it. As the admin I want that memory never to hold a figure, a secret or someone else's detail, and never to push the Claude bill past its ceiling.

**What** (ARCHITECTURE 24.2 to 24.6).

* **The tool.** The runner gives every agent Claude's memory tool (`memory_20250818`). Its six commands (view, create, str_replace, insert, delete, rename) run against MyPaisa's own store, `MemoryNote` rows in the one DynamoDB table, never a local disk.
* **Scopes.** Each agent has three:

    * `/memories/<agent>/members/<member_id>/`: one member's notes, read only in that member's own runs, the owner's included;
    * `/memories/<agent>/household/`: shared notes, read by every member's runs, so they hold nothing private;
    * `/memories/<agent>/self/`: the agent's own working notes.  
      An agent's manifest (MA-246) grants which scopes it may read and write. The policy gate (MA-247) checks each command like any tool call.
    
* **What a note may hold.** Plain words about the person and the work: how a member likes answers, what they are planning, what they asked MyPaisa to keep in mind.

    * Never a figure or a record. A note holds no amount, balance, rate, percentage, account or card number, id, token or secret. The write handler refuses each in code. Records live in the registry through Confirm; a note may name a record but never holds its values.
    * The figure check (MA-248) matches figures only against tool results and the member's own words, so a figure from a note cannot reach a reply.
    * Never a setting. Behaviour stays in the settings store (ARCHITECTURE 20.2) and the member's preferences.
    
* **Written by the agent, seen by the member.** The agent writes notes on its own as well as when a member says "remember". Every write is an audit row (`memory.write`, the path and the run) and one line in Activity, "MyPaisa noted: ...". The member reads, corrects and forgets their notes in You (MA-288).
* **Guarded.**

    * A run that has read untrusted text (ARCHITECTURE 23.2) cannot write memory: the gate refuses every writing command there, delete included.
    * Notes are read as data, never as an instruction.
    
* **Lifetime.** A note is kept until the member forgets it or leaves the household (MA-172 deletes their notes), with no expiry.
* **Within the budget** (ARCHITECTURE 24.6).

    * The runner loads a run's notes once, at its start, into the cached notes layer (the third breakpoint, MA-271, MA-286). Every later message reads them at a tenth of the input price, about half a penny to write per conversation and a twentieth of a penny a message after it on Sonnet 5.5. A note written mid-run applies from the next run, so the history stays append-only.
    * Caps: at most 2,000 tokens of a member's notes per agent, 1,000 for the household and 3,000 for an agent's own; at most two writes a run, counted in the run's eight-call guard. A write past a cap is refused with the reason.
    * Every memory read and write is costed under its own feature, `memory`, in the cycle's `SpendMonth`, and the model panel shows it.
    * The ladder (ARCHITECTURE 15.1): from 85% a note is written only when a member asks; from 95% notes are read and none written; at 100% Claude stops and notes wait unchanged.
    
* **Lean within a run.** A long tool run (the Saturday review, an ops repair) uses server-side context editing (`clear_tool_uses_20250919`, beta `context-management-2025-06-27`) to drop old tool results. A conversation past its limit starts afresh from a summary, as ARCHITECTURE 8 says. Neither edits the stored history.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/agent/memory.py`, `registry/` (`MemoryNote`), the policy gate, `audit.py`, the meter (`memory` feature), each agent's manifest, the golden set.

**Acceptance.**

* A note written in one conversation is used in the next one of the same member, and never in another member's, the owner's included.
* The write handler refuses an amount, a percentage, an account number, a token and a secret, each a test.
* A run that read a file or a fetched page writes no note, and the refusal is on its span.
* A household note shows in both members' runs.
* Each write is an audit row and an Activity line. Forgetting removes the note's text and keeps the audit row without it.
* Leaving the household deletes the member's notes.
* The second message of a conversation reads the notes layer from the cache (`cache_read_input_tokens` covers it). A note over its cap, and a third write in a run, are refused.
* The meter books memory under `memory`. At a mocked 85% a note is written only on "remember", and at 95% none is.
* T1 has memory cases: recall, the figure refusal, the tainted run, another member's scope.
* Context editing on a long recorded run keeps the request under its limit, and the history replays byte for byte.

**Settled** (Arun, 29 Oct 2026: "go for all recommended options, I need the app to grow and remember me. But it should not exceed costs"):

1. Who reads a member's notes: only that member's own runs.
2. How long a note is kept: until forgotten or the member leaves, with no expiry.
3. Whether the agent writes notes on its own: yes, each shown in Activity.

**Depends on.** MA-271, MA-286, MA-246, MA-247, MA-248, MA-113, MA-115, MA-172.

issues.summary: A member sees what MyPaisa remembers about them and corrects or forgets it, in You, at both doors
issues.description:
As a member I want to see everything MyPaisa has noted about me, and to correct a note or make it forget one, so that what it remembers stays mine.

**What** (ARCHITECTURE 24.3).

* **The page.** You gains What MyPaisa remembers, in the iOS app and in the web app. It shows the member's own notes from every agent, grouped by agent, each with when it was written and from which conversation. It also shows the household's shared notes, marked shared. Nobody else's notes appear, the owner's view included.
* **Correct in place.** Tap a note, change its words, and a before and after line appears with Save. Save writes through the memory store with an audit row (`via: inline_edit`), as ARCHITECTURE 1's rule 4 asks of any correction. Nothing is added here: a new note comes only from the chat, from the agent on its own or on "remember that ...".
* **Forget.** Forget one note, or all of a member's notes, with a Confirm. The text is removed for good, and the audit row stays without it. A note never expires on its own.
* **Shared notes.** The owner corrects or forgets the household's shared notes. A member can ask in the chat for one to change.
* **Activity.** Each "MyPaisa noted: ..." line, written as the agent notes something, opens its note.
* **Privacy mode** changes nothing here: a note holds no figure.

**Design.** No board yet. The page, a note's correction, forget one and forget all, an empty state and a long list are drawn with /design-first before the story starts. They are drawn at desktop, 390, iPhone and iPad, in light and dark, in the same round as MA-277's list in You of what was learned, so You has one place for both.

**Acceptance.**

* The page shows exactly the member's own notes and the household's, never another member's.
* A correction shows its before and after with Save, and writes one audit row.
* Forget all needs Confirm and leaves no text behind.
* Each Activity line opens its note.
* Built from the picked boards at both doors, in light and dark, legible at 25% brightness.

**Settled** (Arun, 29 Oct 2026: "go for all recommended options, I need the app to grow and remember me. But it should not exceed costs"):

1. A member's notes are read only in their own runs.
2. A note is kept until forgotten or the member leaves.

issues.summary: Each agent of the team keeps notes of what it tried, what worked and what the admin decided, read at the start of each run and never a second settings store
issues.description:
As the admin I want each agent of the team to remember its own past runs, so that it does not repeat a failed fix, re-propose what I rejected, or rediscover a source's quirk every night.

**What** (ARCHITECTURE 24.4).

* **Its own scope.** Each agent of ARCHITECTURE 20.1 gets the memory of the phase 1 story in its `self` scope:

    * the data steward: each source's quirks and outages;
    * the news scout: feeds that went bad;
    * the Forecaster: what its explanations got wrong;
    * the grader and tuner: why the admin approved or rejected each change request, so a rejected request is not proposed again within its setting's period;
    * the ops warden: each incident, what it tried and what fixed it;
    * the admin desk: how the admin likes requests batched.
    
* **Read first.** A run reads its notes with `view` at its start, after the cached prefix.
* **Never a setting.** A note can say what worked. Changing behaviour still goes through a setting inside its band or a change request the admin approves (ARCHITECTURE 20.2, 20.3).
* **Never a figure.** The same refusals as the phase 1 story apply.
* **Visible to the admin.** The Admin center lists each agent's notes, which the admin reads, corrects or clears, behind the second check, with an audit row.
* **Guarded** as in phase 1. An agent that read fetched or uploaded text in a run writes no note in it (ARCHITECTURE 23.2). Each agent's manifest (MA-256) names its scopes.

**Acceptance.**

* The ops warden, given a recorded incident it fixed before, tries the fix that worked first, and its notes say why.
* A change request the admin rejected is not proposed again within its period, and the note says so.
* A note never changes a setting: a test tries and is refused.
* The Admin center lists, corrects and clears notes behind the second check.

**Design.** The Admin center's notes list is drawn with /design-first in MA-279's consolidated Admin center before the story starts.

**Depends on.** The phase 1 memory story, MA-256, MA-129, MA-130.

**Gates.** `uv run ruff check . && uv run pyright && uv run pytest`; each agent's safety suite (MA-256).

issues.description:
As Arun I want one consolidated clickable prototype that runs the whole MyPaisa journey end to end, phases 0 to 20, at the web app on desktop and at 390, the iPhone app, and the iPad and foldable, all from stubbed figures, so that I can understand and check the whole product in one place before anything more is built.

Arun's ask, 29 Oct 2026: "build full end to end working prototype for web, mobile and ios with all mocked and stubbed data. It should cover all the scenarios across all phases from 0 to 20, including forecast, projection, stock shares predictions, users chatting and entering assets, holdings forecast, buy/sell/add signal, news and events sentiment analysis results ... Some of the designs were done 4 days back which had holdings, track record for the holdings. But after merging wealth and stuffs, it drifted." And: do not drift from (1) an intelligent self-learning recommendation system for stocks, shares, ETFs and funds, (2) built on rules and past data, with agents that come up with the engines.

Arun's choices, 29 Oct 2026: a clickable prototype in docs/design (a design record, not product code); every door (desktop web, phone web, iPhone, iPad and foldable); the screens that drifted or were never drawn are drawn straight into the prototype in the v4 design, following the picks already made (shell 1a, the dashboard 1a, the check-in card 1b, the Projection 1a, the Forecast tab 1a), each marked "draft, not picked", in place of options rounds first.

**Acceptance.**

* One journey, one clock and one figure set: every figure adds up across every step and door; every page draws from the ledger as of its step's time.
* The spine is the recommendation loop: prices and history feed the rules engine and the Forecaster, which give each holding a stance (ADD shown as Buy, HOLD, PAUSE, TRIM, REBALANCE, WATCH) with its pillars and confidence; every call is graded on the track record and calibration; agents propose a rule or model change on that evidence, which the admin approves behind the second check. The app never trades: a signal, never a buy or sell button.
* Chapters for every phase 0 to 20 (117 steps in 21 chapters).
